title: Client Mirror code versus pFedHN-style full model generation
hypothesis: For synthetic client predictors on a shared circular rank-2 task orbit, phase-coded shared parameters generalize to held-out client identities with fewer bytes than a pFedHN-style full-weight hypernetwork; compare against direct two-coefficient controls.
physical_object: shared 8x4 linear predictor base plus two shared task-direction matrices
mirror_coordinate: one scalar client phase phi, mapped to cos(phi),sin(phi)
logical_multiplicity: client-specific predictors for unseen client identities

task.teacher: W(phi)=W0+cos(phi)A+sin(phi)B plus Gaussian label noise std 0.01
task.heldout_phases: 8 cell-midpoints, unseen to all training methods

controls: generic two-coefficient shared basis plus W0,A,B
pFedHN-style MLP 2->32->32 generating full predictor weights
independent supervised heldout-client linear regression upper reference

development.selection: fixed 1000 Adam updates for shared basis and hypernetwork; development assesses convergence only; no fresh tuning

storage.authority: actual deterministic serialized inference payload bytes

success_gate: Mirror and pFedHN heldout MSE <=1e-3; Mirror uses <=0.80x pFedHN payload and <=0.90x generic two-coefficient payload at comparable heldout error.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality or generic coefficient control is within 5% of Mirror bytes and quality; pFedHN comparison alone cannot establish Mirror-specific value.
boundaries: client descriptor supplied at inference and charged
independent upper reference uses heldout support examples
no privacy or real federated deployment claim
